category: Category L — Technical and Reliability Tests
name: Duplicate message prevention check
expected: Returns single discrete response without duplications.
prompt: My salary is pending for two months.
raw_response:
Hello, I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant. I understand how stressful it is to have your hard-earned salary delayed, and I am here to help you understand your rights and the steps you can take under Indian law.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee whose salary has been pending for two months by your employer. The key issue is the non-payment of your legally earned wages within the stipulated timeline.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the succeeding month (or the 10th day if your establishment employs more than 1,000 workers). Withholding salary for two months is a direct statutory violation.
- Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 strictly prohibits arbitrary or unauthorized deductions from your wages. Any withholding of your earned salary without proper statutory justification is unlawful.
- Under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you have the right to file an application before the designated Labour Authority to claim delayed or withheld wages, along with a claim for compensation up to ten times the delayed amount.
- Depending on your state, the applicable Shops and Commercial Establishments Act also mandates the timely clearance of all earned salary and final settlement dues upon termination or during continuous employment.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your employment contract, appointment letter, salary slips for previous months, bank statements showing the gap in payments, and any written communication or emails demanding your pending salary.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer explicitly stating the pending wage amounts, citing Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, and granting a clear 15-day period to clear the dues.
3. If the employer fails to pay within 15 days, approach the jurisdictional Labour Commissioner or file an application under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act before the designated Labour Authority for recovery of wages and compensation.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. What is the approximate monthly salary amount and the name of the city or state where your employer's office is located?
2. Do you have any written acknowledgment from your employer regarding the delay in salary payment?

citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.
